content: Habits formed in the green days of youth become as unyielding as iron in old age.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Shao cheng ruo tian xing (少成若天性) — Book of Rites
explanation: A young sapling can be easily trained to grow straight with a gentle piece of twine. But once the trunk thickens into an ancient oak, no crane on earth can straighten its crooked spine. The small habits you practice today are carving the permanent statue of who you will be.
practicalInsight: Examine your morning and evening rituals. Eliminate one careless micro-habit before it calcifies into your destiny.
reflectionPrompt: What habitual shortcut are you indulging today that is quietly cementing into a flaw you will regret tomorrow?
